improvedVsOld: Clearly better than the old text. The old text kept English state names (« pour Tasmania »), used stiffer calques and was missing many units. The new French reads native almost everywhere: idiomatic imperatives, glossary-consistent terms (caravan park and holiday park glossed once, aire de vidange, State Forests, Total Fire Ban, PVT register) and native exonyms (Nouvelle-Galles du Sud, Australie-Méridionale, Centre rouge, Adélaïde). Typography is right: NBSP before colons and units, ’ apostrophes, « » quotes, decimal commas, « $ AU » where the English writes A$. Automated checks over all 1,364 changed keys found no em dashes and no offline-map claims; every « sans réseau » refers to place details or saved confirmations, which the guide allows. Markup and placeholders match the English byte for byte, including the 51 link-only restorations. Numbers, prices, dates and macrons and other diacritics (Uluṟu, Kata Tjuṯa) are intact. Minor patterns that are not blocking: « comté (shire) » is used instead of municipalité in a few free-camping units; « outback » is lowercase twice (camping-water-planning tips[1], driving-with-road-trains s[3].b[0]); and K'gari has a straight apostrophe in 10 units. Upstream issue, not the translator's fault: the English source carries auto-linker errors that the French faithfully copies. These are « Kangaroo Island » (how-to-plan-trip-aussiecamps s[3].b[0], bus-train-costs s[5].b[1]), « Parks Victoria » splitting the agency name (great-ocean-road s[4].b[0], s[7].b[3]) and « Queensland Rail » (bus-train-costs s[2].b[0]). They should be fixed in en.json and then propagated.

Ne vous baignez jamais, ne videz pas votre poisson et ne campez pas au bord de l’eau en zone à crocodiles, et respectez chaque panneau d’avertissement.

failingUnits.current: …Ne généralisez jamais la règle d’un État en vitesse de remorquage valable pour tout le pays.

failingUnits.problem: « comptabilisés d’un État à l’autre » is ambiguous and could be read as 'counted differently per state'. The English means demerit points are shared across states.

failingUnits.current: Les règles des réserves municipales varient énormément d’une collectivité locale à l’autre. Dormir sur une aire de repos, permis dans un comté, sera interdit dans le suivant : seuls les panneaux font foi.

improvedVsOld:
Overall the new text is clearly better. The diff has 986 changed values. Of these, 281 change only spacing or apostrophes (non-breaking spaces before punctuation, typographic apostrophes), and 705 are rewritten. I read all 705 rewritten units against EN, covering every title, description, heading, FAQ item, UI and consent string, price-table row and note, source label, and rules, fines or prices paragraph, plus nearly all other body text and tips.

What improved:
- Island names are now native per the fr-only catalog (île du Nord, île du Sud, île Stewart (Rakiura)).
- First mentions of DOC, NZTA, ACC, MBIE, Stats NZ, Metlink, GeoNet and rāhui carry glosses.
- Glossary terms are used consistently (holiday park with gloss, freedom camping with gloss, self-contained, aire de vidange, zone blanche, frais d’abandon, rachat de franchise).
- Titles are SEO-led and follow the '<sujet> en Nouvelle-Zélande : <angle>' pattern.
- The privacy page was fixed. In the old FR, sections 4 to 6 were shifted against EN (for example, 'Conservation et contrôle' stood under 'Website analytics'). They are now aligned, and the new analytics and consent text is accurate (13-month _ga cookies, 14-month retention, Google Ireland and Google LLC).

Automated checks, all clean:
- No em dashes.
- No 'tu'.
- No English left untranslated beyond protected or glossary terms.
- No new offline-map claims; the only 'hors connexion' hits are pre-existing unchanged text that mirrors EN 'offline app' and offline search.
- Every number, date, price and currency matches EN. 'NZ$110 to NZ$180' became 'de 110 à 180 $ NZ'; times use the 24-hour format (23 h, 20 h 45).
- Macrons are intact (Kaikōura, Wānaka, Taupō, Tākaka, rāhui, māori).
- No data-guide links or placeholders appear in the changed units, and none were lost.

Minor notes, not scored below 4:
- The volcanic-safety title moves Tongariro, Ruapehu and Rotorua into the description.
- The domestic-flights title adds '2026', which the dated-page rule in the style guide allows.
- The Cook Strait title becomes 'Ferry Wellington-Picton', which is accurate for both operators.
- One plain space remains in '330 ml'.
- Some articles still say 'West Coast' or 'Coromandel' without 'côte Ouest' or 'péninsule', which the style guide allows on first mention.
